solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New performer's impression, involving tuba playing

indicators.note: something involving another takes it in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a dent is an impression pressed into a surface

indicators.note: an instrument being played is set in motion, so the letters of the instrument's name are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the orchestra makes a mark by taking up the tuba.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutant is someone making a first public appearance, such as a performer new to the stage.

clue.text: End of novel possessed rising children's author

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, so the letters run in the opposite order
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word
had means possessed or owned

explanation.surface: The ending of a novel had a children's writer on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole charade is turned upward, so the final letter of novel ends up last.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and Matilda, famous children's books.

clue.text: Composer initially ready to enter piece with half a score

indicators.note: to enter means the letter goes inside the word for piece

parts.note: a bit is a piece

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of ready
a score is twenty, so half of it is ten

explanation.surface: A composer is about to start a piece, having half the score written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' reads as written music, but here it is the number twenty. Benjamin Britten was a 20th-century English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten, who wrote Peter Grimes, is a famous example of a composer.

clue.text: Hard luck over code on website, one difficult to deal with

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means sitting above, so the first piece is written on top of the next

parts.note: tough is a sympathetic exclamation, as in 'tough luck'
a cookie is a small piece of data a website stores on your device

explanation.surface: Bad luck strikes over some website code that proves troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' tempts as the cricket O, but here it only places the first piece above the second in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough cookie is a resilient, hard-headed person who is not easily managed or beaten.

clue.text: Cloth on table mostly helpful after pot overturned

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the helpful piece is written second, following the overturned pot
something overturned is flipped over, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: kind means helpful or considerate

explanation.surface: A cloth on the table proves handy after a pot is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the reversed pot first, with the shortened helpful word following it.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a cloth square laid on the table for wiping hands and mouth at meals.

clue.text: Conserve black doorpost

parts.note: jam is a fruit conserve
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark preserve is smeared on the frame of a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side post of a door or window frame.

clue.text: French friends start to swear in an inappropriate manner

parts.note: amis is French for friends

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: French pals begin cursing at the wrong moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss as an adverb means wrongly or improperly, as in 'take it amiss'.

clue.text: Threatening figures beg money freely

indicators.note: freely means without restriction, so the letters are allowed to move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Intimidating characters openly demand cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogeymen are imaginary monsters or feared people used to frighten, so they are menacing figures.

clue.text: Verse originally heard about in Kyoto University

indicators.note: originally points to the start of things, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A poem was first heard around Kyoto's university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks as if it applies only to 'heard', but it governs all five words that follow; Kyoto fits the Japanese verse form nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of three lines, so it is a kind of verse.

clue.text: What correspondent may be doing — a job overseas?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sending letters by mail
second meaning: an appointment to a position, often abroad

explanation.surface: A foreign correspondent's work abroad is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one newspaper reporter, but the letter-writer sense of correspondent gives the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes letters is busy mailing them, and a diplomat or reporter sent abroad receives an overseas appointment of that name.

clue.text: Queen involved in attempt to reform cheat

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up within it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a shot is an attempt
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
to change is to reform

explanation.surface: The Queen is drawn into a bid to reform a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' looks like an anagram signal, but it is simply a synonym piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To short-change is to give someone less than is due, so to cheat them.

clue.text: Composer OK with Sky TV broadcast about tea

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the drink
broadcast means scattered about, like seed, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be rearranged
chai is tea, especially spiced Indian tea

explanation.surface: A satellite channel agrees to broadcast a documentary about tea with a Russian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as a TV term in the surface, matching Sky TV, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky was the Russian Romantic composer of Swan Lake and The Nutcracker.

clue.text: Writhing idiot finally ignored sharp pain

indicators.note: the final letter is ignored, so it is left off the end of the word

parts.note: a twit is an idiot
a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone writhes as a fool, finally disregarded, feels a stab of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisting is contorting the body, much the same as writhing or squirming.

clue.text: Opportunity to succeed and do well at first

parts.note: to win is to succeed
taken as written after the joining word 'and'

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning of the word, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Advice that a chance to succeed means doing well from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' simply joins two charade pieces here.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a limited period of opportunity, as in a window for talks.

clue.text: More than ever conceals this hydrocarbon

indicators.note: something concealed sits inside, so the letters are found running through the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of More, through than and into ever

explanation.surface: Something now conceals more than ever before.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a simple gaseous hydrocarbon with two carbon atoms, found in natural gas.

clue.text: Ring to cancel American

parts.note: to annul is to cancel
US is short for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: Phone an American to call off a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb meaning to phone, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulus is a ring-shaped figure, the region between two concentric circles.

clue.text: Representative figures dismissing European position

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: statues are figures representing people
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Elected representatives sack a European official from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representative figures' suggests politicians, but it means sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank, that is, a social or professional position.

clue.text: No ketchup is distributed in poor eatery?

definitions.note: the question mark flags 'poor' as meaning for the poor

indicators.note: things distributed are handed out in a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, every letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheap café's poor showing: no ketchup is handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor eatery' reads as a bad restaurant, but it means an eatery for poor people.
explanation.definitionFit: A soup kitchen serves free meals to the needy, so it is a place where the poor eat.

clue.text: University favoured suppressing second disruption

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: a pet project or pet hate is a favoured one
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A favoured university silences a second protest.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a disturbance or disruption to normal order, as in a stomach upset.

clue.text: Privy to round inside pub

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the circle shape goes into the other piece

parts.note: an inn is a pub
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone in the know about a round of drinks in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in on a secret means sharing knowledge of it, which is to be privy to it.

clue.text: Investigate popular religious group, limiting power

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: limiting means hemming in on both sides, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Authorities look into a fashionable cult that curbs power.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, which is to investigate.

clue.text: Dior's refusal to entertain latest items in completely artificial synthetic material

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so the refusal holds the selected letters

parts.note: Christian Dior was French, and non is French for no

indicators.note: the latest items are the final ones, so the last letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the final letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A fashion house refuses anything fake, rejecting man-made fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Dior stands for a French speaker, so the refusal is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a man-made polymer fibre, a classic synthetic material for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Achieved nothing as popular destination

definitions.note: go-to used as a noun, the place everyone turns to

parts.note: got means achieved or obtained
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone got nowhere trying to become a favourite holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-to is the favoured place or resource that people habitually turn to first.

clue.text: Introduces our group to woman's crime

parts.note: us refers to our own group
her refers to a woman
the 's is read as 'is', and a sin is a crime or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Our gang introduces a woman to a life of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s looks possessive but is read as 'is' joining HER to the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher in is to introduce or herald, as an attendant shows guests into a room.
